ocr_text: Arthur M. Pendleton, a clerk employed in an insurance brokerage on Euclid Avenue, was brought before Magistrate Higgins this morning charged with unlawfully pawning an overcoat belonging to his employer. When interrogated Pendleton confessed that he had pawned the heavy winter coat for four dollars at Goldsteins pawnshop on Water street. When asked by the magistrate why he had committed the offense Pendleton replied through tears that he had desired to purchase an engagement ring for his sweetheart Miss Vance before her family departed for the lakeside summer cottage. The magistrate ordered Pendleton to make full restitution within thirty days.
facts: A clerk pawned a winter overcoat in the middle of June for four dollars
He needed the four dollars to buy an engagement ring for his fiancée
The magistrate ordered restitution within thirty days
human_need: The desperate pressure to look financially secure to impress someone you love
modern_mirror: Taking out high-interest Buy-Now-Pay-Later loans to fund holiday gifts and engagement trips

ocr_text: HEART TO HEART TALKS WITH AUNT MARGARET. Anxious Reader writes: I have received three long letters during the past fortnight from a gentleman who sat beside me at a lawn fete in June, though he has not yet paid a formal visit to my parents. Should I reply to his third letter or remain silent? Answer: You must under no circumstances reply. A gentleman who values your good name will knock upon your father's parlor door before filling your postbox with idle flatteries.

ocr_text: ADVICE FOR MODERN HOMES. Perplexed Housewife writes: My mother-in-law visits our cottage every Thursday and rearranges the bric-a-brac in the front parlor, stating that young housekeepers today have no eye for order. How can I protest without causing open war? Answer: You must say nothing with your lips. Return the vases quietly to their original places after her departure. A quiet hand wins more domestic battles than a sharp tongue.
facts: A housewife asked how to stop her visiting mother-in-law from rearranging her parlor every Thursday
The mother-in-law claimed modern young housekeepers had no sense of order
The columnist advised silent boundary enforcement: put everything back after she leaves without arguing
